newsitem.title: USA: Chronimed, Orphan say terminate agreement.
newsitem.headline: Chronimed, Orphan say terminate agreement.

text.p: Orphan Medical Inc and Chronimed Inc said they terminated an agreement under which Chronimed had exclusive rights to market and distribute certain Orphan Medical products.
As a result of the termination, Orphan said it will take a charge against earnings of at least $2.1 million in its second quarter ended June 30.
The termination agreement calls for Orphan to pay cash, royalties and common stock to Chronimed totalling $2.5 million over 12 to 24 months, the companies said.

"We have reached this agreement because it has become apparent to both parties that the majority of Orphan Medical's products require distribution to markets beyond the direct-to-patient distribution channel, which is Chronimed's forte," said John Bullion, Orphan chief executive.
"Termination of this agreement allows Orphan Medical to take full control over its product portfolio," he said.

The distribution deal had been in effect since Orphan's July 1994 spinoff from Chronimed and gave Chronimed exclusive domestic marketing and distribution rights to products transferred by Chronimed to Orphan upon the spinoff.
"Chronimed may be considered in the future for distribution of products that particularly fit its competencies," Bullion said.
Orphan and Chronimed are both in the healthcare business.
